slides.title: Is there a gap in your leg protection?
slides.sub: Shin guards, knee pads and a 15 second check

slides.title: Protection has two jobs
slides.body: It has to resist a slicing edge and spread a blunt impact. Cut resistant fabric does the first. A hard shell or dense foam pad does the second.

slides.title: Football shin guards work for training
slides.body: Wear them over a cut resistant layer, never instead of one. Check your federation's rules before you race in them too.

slides.title: The coverage chain and its two weak points
slides.caption: Knee pad, shin guard and boot should overlap, with the two common gaps marked in orange.

slides.title: Fit knee pads with the knee bent
slides.body: Bend to your cornering angle, centre the pad on the cap, then stand up. If it moves more than a little, the strap is too loose or the pad too big.

slides.title: Check for gaps before you step on
slides.body: In your lowest skating position, check the boot line, sock top, guard to knee and kneecap. The gap is almost always at the boot line.

slides.title: When a knock needs more than ice
slides.body: See a doctor or physiotherapist for sharp pain, clear swelling, numbness or if you cannot bear weight. A deep blade cut needs attention the same day.
